status: provisional static appraisal pending dynamic profiler evidence from issue #184

classes.python-bound: Material algorithmic work executes in CPython rather than merely dispatching to compiled kernels.
classes.numpy-scipy-bound: Python primarily orchestrates NumPy/SciPy vectorized or sparse native kernels.
classes.blas-lapack-bound: Dominant numerical work is delegated to mature BLAS/LAPACK-backed linear algebra.
classes.sklearn-native-bound: Dominant hot loops are implemented in sklearn-owned Cython/C/C++ code.
classes.external-native-bound: Dominant algorithm is implemented by an external native library such as liblinear or libsvm.
classes.mixed-boundary-heavy: Substantial work spans Python orchestration and one or more compiled substrates; boundary/allocation/fusion effects are plausible optimization targets.

rows.note: Do not describe the sklearn implementation as pure Python: Python coordinates optimization while substantial numerical work executes in compiled kernels.
A Flow loss here is primarily a comparison against a mature native solver, not against interpreted Python.
The relevant baseline is libsvm plus sklearn integration overhead. Rewriting Python wrappers alone cannot explain kernel-level performance.
This is a direct compiled-code comparison; Flow wins or losses should be attributed to implementation/code generation rather than removal of Python loops.

rows.native_dependency: sklearn Cython trees plus ensemble orchestration
rows.note: Individual trees are native; orchestration, parallelism, aggregation and allocation remain separate layers and are legitimate whole-program targets.
The strong small-workload Flow result is consistent with reducing dispatch/allocation around simple vectorized arithmetic; it is not evidence that sklearn runs GaussianNB as Python scalar loops.

rows.native_dependency: sklearn Cython kernels with optimized numerical primitives
rows.note: This is principally a native algorithm implementation contest. Digits parity is unresolved, so its timing cannot support a competitive claim.

rows.native_dependency: LAPACK/SciPy/NumPy linear algebra depending on solver
rows.note: Flow should normally preserve mature decomposition kernels and compete on orchestration, specialization, allocation and deployment unless a replacement kernel is demonstrably better.
Interpret results by the selected solver. A whole-estimator win does not imply Flow has outperformed BLAS itself.
The current large Flow loss identifies a concrete native implementation/code-generation optimization target rather than generic Python overhead.

rows.native_dependency: SciPy/BLAS/LAPACK least-squares path for dense data
rows.note: The headline result is end-to-end estimator timing. It must not be presented as proof that Flow's underlying linear algebra kernel is faster than LAPACK.
The current Flow loss suggests kernel construction/solve/integration needs profiling before any architectural performance claim.
